resources.string: A crosshair that sits on top of everything and never eats a tap.
Android needs this before anything can be drawn on top of another app.
Draws the crosshair from an accessibility service, one layer above normal app overlays. Useful if another floating app keeps covering it. Optional.
Off by default, so the floating button stays wherever you drop it, middle of the screen included. Turn on to have it spring back to the nearest side.
Brings the overlay back on its own when the phone restarts.
Tap the floating sigil to open the tuning panel.
Drag the sigil anywhere on screen, including the middle.
Long press it to show or hide the crosshair without opening anything.
The crosshair is always click through, at every opacity including 100%. Taps land on the app underneath.
Drag the crosshair to place it. Tap it once to snap back to center.
Android 12 and newer block taps that land on the crosshair when a pass-through overlay is more than 80% opaque. Turn on max priority mode for solid 100%, or drop to 80%.
Keeps the crosshair on screen while you use other apps.
Draws the crosshair one layer above normal app overlays.
Turn this on only if you want the crosshair to outrank other floating apps. It draws the crosshair and nothing else. It does not read the screen, record input, or collect any data.
Find Crosshair in this list and turn it on.
Import any PNG, WebP or JPG. Transparent PNGs work best. Images are copied into the app, so moving or deleting the original afterwards is fine.
Nothing imported yet. Tap + to add an image.
